f.title: Use OCMQs to support, not replace, review of individual AE terms and other groupings
f.statement: OCMQs give a standard grouping of adverse event terms to help identify potential safety issues during review of clinical trial adverse event data. They are not intended to replace review of the individual reported adverse event terms or of other available and appropriate groupings during clinical trial safety analysis.
f.applicability: FDA internal review practice (CDER OND, MAPP 6025.8): NME NDAs, original 351(a) BLAs, relevant supplements and other applications reviewed with OCMQs; informative for applicants, not binding on them
f.processes: Signal detection; Signal management; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote:
The purpose of the OCMQs is to provide a standard grouping of adverse event
          (AE) terms designed to help identify potential safety issues during review of
          clinical trial AE data. OCMQs are not intended to replace review of individual
          reported AE terms or other available and appropriate groupings of AE terms
          during clinical trial data safety analysis.

f.title: Algorithmic OCMQs add criteria beyond single AE terms (term combinations, labs, con-meds, history, timing)
f.statement: Some OCMQs contain an algorithmic component that uses additional information to identify safety signals: combinations of adverse event terms instead of a single term, laboratory data, concomitant medications, medical history or timing information. Each algorithm is a series of criteria, and patients who meet the specified criteria are considered to have met the requirement of the algorithm. The Targeted Analysis Guides on the internal Standard Safety Tables and Figures site describe each algorithmic OCMQ.

f.title: Narrow OCMQ scope: include terms indicating that the OCMQ condition occurred
f.statement: The Narrow category of an OCMQ indicates that the condition occurred. It includes adverse event terms that are near synonyms of the OCMQ, subgroups of it, terms that specify an etiology for it, and terms that ensure its occurrence.
f.applicability: FDA internal review practice (CDER OND, MAPP 6025.8): NME NDAs, original 351(a) BLAs, relevant supplements and other applications reviewed with OCMQs; informative for applicants, not binding on them

rows.actor: OND clinical reviewers and OCMQ Steering Committee
rows.quote:
Narrow Category: Indicates that the OND Custom Medical Query (OCMQ) occurred.

    •   Adverse events (AEs) that are near synonyms of the OCMQ (e.g., Preferred Term
        PT Abdominal Discomfort in OCMQ Abdominal Pain, and PT Blood Glucose
        Increased in OCMQ Hyperglycemia)

    •   AEs that are subgroups of the OCMQ (e.g., PT Anaemia Neonatal in OCMQ
        Anemia).

    •   AEs that specify an etiology for the OCMQ (e.g., PT Uraemic Pruritus in OCMQ
        Pruritus).

    •   AEs that ensure the occurrence of the OCMQ (e.g., PT Aortic Rupture in OCMQ
        Hemorrhage).
rows.review_note: Level Informative 2026-11-26 (Venkat chose option A, issue #634): FDA reviewer practice, not an applicant duty; FDA wording for its staff: Mandatory. Pass 3 double-check 2026-11-25: quote proves statement, level and actor fit, review-practice framing kept.

f.title: Broad OCMQ scope: include terms reasonably suggestive that the OCMQ condition may have occurred
f.statement: The Broad category of an OCMQ is reasonably suggestive that the condition may have occurred. It includes adverse event terms that may indicate the condition; terms giving laboratory, radiologic or other diagnostic results reasonably suggestive of it, including ambiguous results such as "abnormal"; terms reasonably suggestive of but not required by the OCMQ; and, for infectious-disease OCMQs, terms indicating carrier status.
f.applicability: FDA internal review practice (CDER OND, MAPP 6025.8): NME NDAs, original 351(a) BLAs, relevant supplements and other applications reviewed with OCMQs; informative for applicants, not binding on them

rows.actor: OND clinical reviewers and OCMQ Steering Committee
rows.quote:
Broad Category: Reasonably suggestive that the OCMQ may have occurred.

    •   AEs that may indicate the presence of the OCMQ (e.g., PT Osteopenia in OCMQ
        Osteoporosis).

    •   AEs that provide laboratory, radiologic, or other diagnostic test results reasonably
        suggestive of an OCMQ, including AEs with ambiguous results such as
        “abnormal” (e.g., PT Troponin I Increased in OCMQ Myocardial Infarction, and
        PT Blood Glucose Abnormal in OCMQ Hyperglycemia).

    •   AEs reasonably suggestive of the OCMQ, but not required by the OCMQ (e.g.,
        PT Bronchospasm in OCMQ Hypersensitivity).

    •   AEs that indicate a “carrier” status for OCMQ that specify an infectious disease
        (e.g., PT Bacterial Disease Carrier in OCMQ Bacterial Infection).
rows.review_note: Level Informative 2026-11-26 (Venkat chose option A, issue #634): FDA reviewer practice, not an applicant duty; FDA wording for its staff: Mandatory. Pass 3 double-check 2026-11-25: quote proves statement, level and actor fit, review-practice framing kept.

f.title: Use the MedDRA SOCs to identify congenital and pregnancy-related events excluded from OCMQs
f.statement: Congenital, familial or genetic disorders reported in a clinical trial can be identified with the corresponding MedDRA System Organ Class. Pregnancy, puerperium and perinatal conditions are rare in a typical trial and, when they occur, should be carefully analysed; for trials that investigate pregnancy or breastfeeding, allow these in their eligibility criteria, or include neonatal or infant populations, the Pregnancy, puerperium and perinatal conditions SOC can be used to identify these terms for further analysis.
f.applicability: FDA internal review practice; trials investigating pregnancy or breastfeeding, allowing these in eligibility, or including neonatal or infant populations
f.processes: Signal detection; Signal management; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote:
Any congenital, familial, or genetic disorders reported during a clinical trial can be
identified using the MedDRA System Organ Class for these terms.
8
  Such conditions are quite rare in a typical clinical trial, and when they do occur should be carefully
analyzed. For trials that specifically investigate pregnancy or breastfeeding, that allow these as part of their
eligibility criteria, or that include neonatal or infant populations, the Pregnancy, puerperium and perinatal
conditions MedDRA System Organ Class can be used to identify these terms for further analysis.
